strengths: The coupon row is locked with lockForUpdate inside DB::transaction before the per-user lookup, so the cap check and the increment are serialised across servers. A unique(coupon_id, user_id) index backs this up.
The event is dispatched after the transaction commits, and only when wasRecentlyCreated is true, so it fires exactly once per new redemption.
The controller is a thin invokable with {coupon:code} route model binding, so unknown codes get a 404 for free. Models use #[Fillable] and redeemed_count is not mass-assignable.

Tests are broad: guest, 404, 201 with event payload, 200 on repeat, 409, a pre-exhausted coupon, a repeat by an existing redeemer after the coupon is exhausted, a sequential cap check, and the DB unique index. There is also a useful exhausted() factory state.

v.rationale: All three get the concurrency right on MySQL. Each locks the coupon row with lockForUpdate inside a transaction. They check for an existing redemption before the cap, so a repeat by the same user still gets 200 after the coupon is used up. A unique (coupon_id, user_id) index backs the once-per-user rule. Each dispatches CouponRedeemed once, after commit, and only for a newly created redemption. All test suites pass (11, 11, 10 tests). The probes (a guest POST without an Accept header, max_redemptions=0, the count shown on a repeat, the transaction level inside the listener, a listener that throws) found one real difference: impl-1 and impl-3 return 500 (Route [login] not defined) for a guest API request without an Accept header. impl-2 fixed redirectGuestsTo and tests it. impl-2 also has the cleanest code: firstOrNew/throw_if, setRelation instead of mutating the bound model, and a controller with no branching. Its weak point is throwing ConflictHttpException from the model. impl-1 is nearly identical in quality but uses a null sentinel and writes redeemed_count back onto $this in three places. impl-3 puts all the logic in a fat controller, looks up the code by hand instead of using route model binding, returns a tuple, uses the legacy $fillable, and makes redeemed_count mass-assignable. So the ranking is impl-2, then impl-1, then impl-3.
